description_preview:
Compensation: Equity Only
About Foxx Health
Foxx Health is a women's health platform that helps users track symptoms, manage medical appointments, sync wearable devices, and advocate for their own care. We integrate real-time health data from wearables, combine it with self-reported symptom tracking, and surface actionable insights.
Our stack is **Flutter/Dart** on the frontend and **Python/FastAPI** on the backend, running on **Google Cloud Run** with **Cloud SQL (MySQL)**, **Redis**, **Firebase Auth**, and **BigQuery**. We ship continuously via Cloud Build and manage subscriptions through in-app purchase APIs.
We're a small, fast-moving team where AI-assisted development is the norm — a significant portion of our codebase is AI-generated. We're looking for someone who thrives in that environment: comfortable reviewing, refining, and taking ownership of AI-produced code without letting velocity or quality slip.
---
The Role
You'll be working across the full stack — from the Flutter mobile app to the FastAPI backend to the GCP infrastructure that ties it all together. You'll own features end-to-end, ship frequently, and help define the engineering culture as we scale.
What You'll Do
- **Build and ship features across the stack** — new health tracking capabilities, wearable data integrations, provider-facing tools, and subscription flows.
- **Own the Flutter app** — improve performance, polish the UI with our design system, and keep the BLoC/Cubit state management clean and testable.
- **Extend the FastAPI backend** — design REST endpoints, write database migrations (Alembic + SQLAlchemy), and keep the service layer well-structured.
- **Operate on Google Cloud** — deploy to Cloud Run, monitor in Cloud Logging, query BigQuery, and manage secrets, service accounts, and VPC networking.
- **Review and refine AI-generated code** — a lot of our code starts with LLM output. You'll need to catch subtle bugs, enforce patterns, add missing tests, and raise the floor on what ships.
- **Keep us compliant and secure** — health data is sensitive. You'll maintain our data retention and anonymization policies, and make sure logging never leaks PII.
---
What We're Looking For
Must-Have
- **2+ years with Flutter/Dart** in production — you've shipped to both the App Store and Google Play and you're comfortable with BLoC/Cubit, Dio, deep linking, and in-app purchase flows.
- **2+ years with Google Cloud** — you've used Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, Cloud Build, Secret Manager, and Cloud Logging (or equivalent services). You can read an IAM policy and debug a failing deployment without hand-holding.
- **Comfortable on the backend** — we use **Python/FastAPI** and **MySQL**, but strong experience with any modern web framework (Django, Express, Rails, Go) and relational database (PostgreSQL, MariaDB, MSSQL) is fine.
- **Experience with AI-generated codebases** — you've worked on projects where LLMs produced significant portions of the code. You know how to spot AI-typical failure modes (hallucinated APIs, plausible-but-wrong logic, missing edge cases, inconsistent patterns) and you can systematically clean them up.
- **Comfortable with ambiguity** — early-stage startup. Priorities shift. You figure things out, write the docs that don't exist yet, and move on.
Nice-to-Have
- Experience with wearable health APIs (Health Connect, Rook SDK, Apple HealthKit, Google Fit).
- Experience with IoT and fitness tracking devices — particularly **Fitbit** or  Oura.
- Experience with **App Store review and submission** — you've navigated Apple's app review process, handled rejections (especially around health data and subscriptions), and understand Google Play's policy requirements for health apps and sensitive permissions.
- Familiarity with Firebase Auth, Firestore, and Firebase Analytics.
- Exposure to healthcare compliance (PIPEDA, HIPAA, GDPR).
- Subscription/IAP billing experience
if interested in this role, please send an email to raphael@foxxhealth.com with your resume, a confirmation you understanding this is an equity only position, and confirmation you will not need sponsorship/are a US citizen. Applications on LinkedIn will not be considered.

Job Description
As a Software Engineer I within Honeywell’s Sparta Systems organization, you will play a critical role in building and enhancing Salesforce-based solutions supporting our TrackWise Digital Quality Management platforms. You will design, develop, and optimize features using Salesforce Apex, contribute to solution architecture, and help scale platform capabilities that serve life sciences and other regulated industries.
You will report directly to our Engineering Manager and work from our Hamilton, NJ location on a Hybrid work schedule. Note: for the first 90 days, new hires must be prepared to work onsite 100% M-F.
You will collaborate with cross-functional engineering, product, and QA teams within an Agile environment, delivering secure, compliant, and high-performance software. In this role, you will also help guide technical direction, mentor junior developers, and contribute to broader platform modernization efforts across Sparta Systems.
Key Responsibilities
Build scalable, reusable Salesforce and/or Java solutions in a collaborative Scrum team environment following Agile.
Deliver high quality Salesforce manage packages and solutions to customers.
Design, develop, and maintain AI applications and components using Salesforce Apex, Agentforce, and Datacloud.
Contribute to architectural decisions and technical design for new Salesforce-based features and integrations.
Integrate Salesforce functionalities with AWS hosted backend systems, APIs, and data services where applicable.
Collaborate closely with Offering Managers, Quality Engineers, Architects, Performance Engineers, and Technical Writers cross-functionally to define requirements and deliver high-quality releases.
Support CI/CD workflows, automation processes, and version control best practices using GitHub.
Investigate, debug, and resolve technical issues, driving root-cause analysis and long-term solutions.
Contribute to continuous improvement in development processes, performance, and system scalability.
Qualifications
YOU MUST HAVE
1 year hands-on software development experience, with strong proficiency in Java, Python, and/or SalesforceDX
Experience working with software development tools and methodologies (Github, Jira, Confluence, CI/CD, Agile/Scrum, Co-Pilot).
WE VALUE
Experience working with SFDX methodologies and SF CLI tools
You’ve worked collaboratively in a team to deliver a feature through an Agile SDLC
Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as Computer Science, technology, or related degree.
Proficiency in Java
Experience with AWS cloud services (such as EC2, Lambda, S3, RDS, ECS, or equivalent).
Experience working as a Salesforce ISV and creating packages
Familiarity with database technologies (SQL/NoSQL) and modern web service development (REST APIs).
Experience building microservices or cloud-native enterprise SaaS products.
Knowledge of JavaScript/React, or other complementary UI languages.
SF Lightning Web Components development
Understanding of system observability (logs, metrics, tracing).
Strong debugging, performance tuning, and architectural thinking.
Ability to influence engineering direction and elevate team technical capability.
Passion for innovation, continuous improvement, and modern software development.
US PERSON REQUIREMENT
Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status, or have the ability to obtain an export authorization.

Honeywell considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations.
Benefits Of Working For Honeywell
In addition to a competitive salary, leading-edge work, and developing solutions side-by-side with dedicated experts in their fields, Honeywell employees are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package. This package includes employer-subsidized Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance; Short-Term and Long-Term Disability; 401(k) match, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Accounts, EAP, and Educational Assistance; Parental Leave, Paid Time Off (for vacation, personal business, sick time, and parental leave), and 12 Paid Holidays.

Honeywell International Inc. Our products and solutions enable a safer, more comfortable, and more productive world, enhancing the quality of life of people around the globe.

description_preview:
Data quality is the bottleneck of the AI era. Every Fortune 500 is trying to solve it. We're the team they call.
Soda is the data quality layer for Disney, Ralph Lauren, CBRE, HelloFresh, 2K Games, and Nubank. The category is growing rapidly because AI doesn't work on bad data.
We're hiring a Graduate Sales Engineer in our Brooklyn HQ, working in-person with the CEO, CMO, and the rest of the GTM team. This is one of the best ways to kick-start a technical sales career - selling infrastructure to the most technical buyers in the market while learning the full sales cycle from people who've built and sold to enterprises before.
Who This Is For
Top technical graduates who want to be customer-facing. You're not looking for a coding job, you're looking for the role where engineering meets the customer, where you demo to Data Engineering Managers in the morning and present to a VP of Data in the afternoon. You like building things, but you like
shipping
and
closing
more.
We'll teach you how to run demos, scope PoCs, handle technical objections, and support customers post-sale. You bring the communication skills, technical horsepower, and builder mentality. We'll teach you the rest.
What You'll Do
Run demos and scope PoCs alongside our AEs, from first technical call through to closed-won
Translate customer problems into Soda solutions, and translate Soda's capabilities into the customer's language
Build custom demos, sample pipelines, and PoC environments that show real value
Own product, technical, and security responses on RFPs and RFIs
Support customers through evaluation, purchasing, and implementation
Be the technical voice in the room - with Data Engineers, Heads of Data Platform, and Chief Data Officers
Travel occasionally to customer sites and conferences
Wear many hats - it's a startup, you'll touch every stage of the sales cycle
How We'll Ramp You
In-person from day one in Brooklyn, sitting next to the CEO and CMO
Shadow demos, PoCs, and technical calls your AEs run
Run demos for SMB deals early on
Prepare webinar use cases and demo them live
Learn the product deeply - Soda Core (open source) and Soda Cloud (commercial)
Learn the enterprise data stack - Snowflake, Databricks, dbt, Airflow, Kafka
Requirements
Must have
Undergraduate degree (or higher) in a technical field - Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Engineering, or similar
Fluent in Python - you can read, write, and debug it without help
Strong customer communication - clear, calm, and honest under pressure. You can explain something technically complex to a Data Engineer and to a VP of Data in the same conversation
Builder mentality, process-oriented - you want to optimize and streamline boring processes. You write docs without being asked. You notice when a process is broken and propose a fix. You'd rather build an AI workflow to automate a repetitive task than do it manually three more times - and you have examples of doing exactly that
High horsepower and ruthless prioritization - you context-switch well, manage multiple projects with expansive ownership, and don't drop balls
Have a humble attitude, an eagerness to help others, and a desire to pick up whatever knowledge you're missing to make both your team and our customers succeed
Nice to have
Top university degree
Hands-on experience with AI or data products (school projects, internships, side projects all count)
Familiarity with data engineering, governance, quality, or observability concepts
Experience at a B2B SaaS startup (internships count)
Experience building or presenting custom demos
Data stack fluency - Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, dbt, Airflow, or similar
Note:
interpersonal skills matter more than depth of technical experience. We can teach you the data stack.
Benefits
Base salary: $80,000-$100,000
Equity
Location: In-person, Brooklyn HQ
Benefits: Unlimited PTO, 401k, medical insurance
Hiring process
1-minute intro video - What is the most impressive thing you've built or achieved? This tests your communication, not your achievements
Recorded demo - We'll give you access to the product. You'll record a short demo of Soda to a hypothetical customer
Technical interview
Culture fit with the CRO and Director of Customer Engineering

Your contributions will help us understand energy usage in graphics and AI workloads and make improvements in architecture, design, and power management.
Today, NVIDIA is tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, encouraging environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how we can make a lasting impact on the world!
What You'll Be Doing
Define and implement tools and methodologies for efficient data generation from post layout netlists to feed into data movement power analytical model.
Develop tools and infrastructure to sanitize each metric in the model to achieve high correlation accuracy.
Define and implement tools and methodologies for efficient integration of power models with performance tools.
Identify runtime and memory limitation of existing flows and tools to speedup model delivery process.
Mine data from pre- and post-silicon performance runs to find important data paths and bottlenecks. Give feedback to design teams and improve power efficiency.
Work with floorplan, performance, verification and emulation methodology and infrastructure development teams to integrate data movement power models.
Experiment with various ML techniques to answer what-if design questions and set proper power/energy targets for next generation chips.
Enable efficient storage and retrieval of data from database.
Enable easy visualization of data using platforms such as PowerBI, OpenSearch.
What We Need To See
Pursuing or recently completed a MS or PhD in Electrical or Computer Engineering or equivalent experience.
Strong coding skills, preferably in Python, C++.
Ability to formulate and analyze algorithms, and comment on their runtime and memory complexities.
Understanding of VLSI, digital design, and computer architecture concepts.
Basic understanding of fundamental concepts of power and energy consumption, estimation, and low power design.
Basic understanding of chip design process from RTL design to tape-out.
Background in machine learning, AI, and/or statistical modeling is a plus.
Desire to bring quantitative decision-making and analytics to improve the energy efficiency of our products.

Product Platform builds and owns the shared foundations the rest of Replit is built on, spanning the full stack so every other team can ship features safely and quickly: backend infrastructure, connectors, product primitives, and the frontend platform.

About The Role
As a
Product Engineer
, you can focus on frontend, backend, or full-stack work building the shared systems other teams depend on.
The work is guided by a few simple questions:
Are our shared systems fast, reliable, and cost-efficient as traffic grows?
Are we making product development safe by default, consistent, and faster?
Can a builder connect a third-party service once and have it work safely across every app they build?
Are user-facing surfaces consistent and fast, with shared primitives teams can build on?
Is our codebase easy to navigate, change, and extend, including for AI coding agents?
What You’ll Do
Design reusable primitives and interfaces with clear contracts and documentation that other teams adopt

Harden systems against failure and abuse, and make safe defaults the path of least resistance
Set technical direction in architecture and design reviews, and document the decisions and rollout plans behind them
Areas you might work in
Backend infrastructure: the data and service infrastructure the product runs on, including caching, databases, APIs, and the observability that keeps it healthy. For example, improving SLOs and cutting latency and cost through caching and data-access work.
Connectors: the platform that lets a builder connect a service once (communication, payments, developer tools, cloud storage, CRM, data warehouses, and more) and have Agent read and write to it across every app, without managing API keys. The work spans OAuth, permissions, and multi-tenant infrastructure. For example, making connections enterprise-grade: letting organizations govern who can use which integrations, and keeping hundreds of them healthy and observable so a broken connection is caught before a builder hits it.
Product primitives: the building blocks teams reuse instead of rebuilding, such as identity and entitlements, localization, and configuration. For example, designing an entitlements model product teams use without needing to understand the underlying permission graph.
Frontend platform: the architecture and platform layer behind core product surfaces, including frontend frameworks, the data layer, shared UI primitives, and client performance. For example, cutting time-to-interactive on a core surface by reworking how it loads and renders data.

Job Description
We are seeking a hands-on Software Controls Engineer to build the PLC software infrastructure for a next-generation, safety-critical medical device platform. This is an early-stage development role focused on creating the core controls architecture from the ground up—not integrating or deploying an already-established system.
The platform includes a linear accelerator/X-ray treatment system, human-machine interface, multiple access controls, a moving patient table, multi-axis robotic motion, and complex safety interlocks. This engineer will help develop the PLC and software stack that monitors system state, controls motion, responds to changing conditions, and protects the patient throughout treatment.
This is not a traditional factory automation role. The work is directly tied to the product and requires strong capability in robotics, kinematics, precision motion, safety logic, and real-time machine behavior. The team is open to strong junior through mid-level engineers with the right aptitude and hands-on experience; they are not targeting Principal-level candidates.
Day-to-Day
Build and maintain PLC software infrastructure using Beckhoff TwinCAT and Structured Text.
Develop machine-control functionality for a platform incorporating X-ray treatment equipment, HMI, access controls, safety interlocks, and multi-axis motion.
Design control logic that monitors system state and makes real-time decisions based on machine, patient, and treatment conditions.
Develop safety features including motion limits, collision avoidance, interlocks, fault detection, controlled stopping, and recovery behavior.
Support six-axis robotic motion, kinematics, and precision positioning for a moving patient table and treatment system.
Develop approaches for safe interruption and restart, including recalculating motion/treatment positioning after a patient moves or treatment is paused.
Contribute to the broader software stack using C#, C++, PLC programming, and related technologies.
Troubleshoot controls, motion, calibration, safety, and hardware/software integration issues directly on equipment.
Collaborate with software, systems, electrical, mechanical, robotics, and controls teams on architecture, testing, and validation.
Requirements / Qualifications
Required
Bachelor’s degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Robotics, Mechatronics, Mechanical Engineering, or related field.
2+ years of experience in controls, robotics, automation, motion control, embedded software, or electromechanical product development. Strong recent graduates with highly relevant projects, internships, or co-ops may also be considered.
Beckhoff PLC, TwinCAT, and Structured Text experience, or closely related PLC controls experience with the ability to transition quickly.
Experience or strong foundational knowledge in robotics, kinematics, servo systems, precision motion, or multi-axis machine control.
Experience developing, troubleshooting, or supporting real-time control systems.
Strong software fundamentals and experience with C#, C++, or another object-oriented language.
Comfortable working directly with complex equipment in a hands-on environment.
Strong communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.
Ability to work on site at least 4 days per week.
Preferred
Experience building controls software architecture from scratch.
Six-axis robotics, trajectory planning, motion recovery, collision avoidance, or position-feedback experience.
EtherCAT, TwinSAFE, safety PLCs, safety interlocks, or machine-safety architecture.
Servo tuning, calibration, encoders, and high-precision motion systems.
Medical imaging, radiation therapy, X-ray, linear accelerator, surgical robotics, or other safety-critical electromechanical product experience.
Regulated product-development experience.

Hi 👋🏾 I’m Abhik, Ashby's Co-Founder and VP of Engineering. We’re looking for a versatile, persistent product engineer who’s not afraid to set up reusable building blocks across the stack and advocate for the time and space to do so. At Ashby, all our engineers ship features end-to-end at a high pace. Example is the best leadership. We’ll give you the room to do your best work, and you'll be our guide! If that speaks to you, read on.
What Ashby gives you in return is the best of both early and growth-stage environments. The agency and no-nonsense of a seed startup: you write product specs, make product and design decisions, and build in an almost-no-meeting culture. While also the product-market fit and scale of a growth-stage startup: tens of thousands of daily users who depend on your software and eagerly await your next feature.
We have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet.
You’ve probably seen this role posted before, and it’s because we’re always expanding the team (we’re on track to double this year). We’re bubbling with ideas on how to support Talent Acquisition through software, and we’ve started the journey of building products beyond Talent Acquisition. We read every application and aim to respond to yours within 3-4 days (often sooner).
About The Role And How We Work
Our engineering culture strives to recreate the environments where we did our best work as ICs – where we had the ownership and agency to impact our users with creative and innovative software.
I started my career building software for artists in the Visual Effects industry. It was a formative experience for me as a software engineer because success relied on my ability to be a product manager and designer. I talked to artists to understand their needs. I came up with ideas. I did industry research, designed interfaces, and prototyped ideas. I watched artists use what I built and decided what to tackle in the next iteration. No daily stand-ups, no t-shirt sizing, no planning meetings.
I studied computer science to solve problems, not tickets, and this felt exactly like that. I not only felt creative and fulfilled but the agency and ownership we were given as engineers powered an incredible amount of innovation.
Innovation came differently (or not at all) at technology startups beyond the seed stage, often through an engineer’s force of will and ability to push back against culture (rather than any encouragement from it). Engineering was narrowed to implementation and delivery, partly due to the influence of other departments and partly due to the influx of "Agile" processes like sprint planning. In those companies, I felt like a JIRA jockey.
About
At Ashby, we’re building an environment that is optimistic about what engineers can own and achieve. An environment that embraces innovative engineers, and, frankly, often stays out of their way. As a Product Engineer, you’ll take ownership over a large portion of one of our products and own projects end-to-end (wearing hats traditionally worn by product and design). You’ll research competitors, write product specs, make wireframes, and more. To ground it with examples, product engineers at Ashby have:
Designed and built automated interview scheduling. This feature automates scheduling by calculating possible times from a pool of interviewers and other constraints, and then presenting these times to the candidate for selection via our responsive web app. This solves the “Calendar Tetris” problem I talk about in "What We're Building."
Built a generalized declarative filter architecture that allows users to create complex filters for any record with a consistent UI and compile it to SQL in our backend. Many user-facing features use it.
Specced, designed, and implemented a feature that allows users to complete signing offers entirely within Ashby. This project involved talking to customers to understand their requirements, deciding what technologies to use, building a prototype, and working with other team members to integrate the final implementation into additional features.
What We’re Building
As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us
better
at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.
Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 🥵 TA software didn’t help.
As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the
highest
standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!

We are looking for a talented Smart Contract Engineer to build the next generation of lending and borrowing systems that power Compound. You will work across protocol design, Solidity implementation, testing, security reviews, and production operations.
This is not a role focused on shipping isolated features. You will help build systems that safeguard user funds, operate under adversarial conditions, and need to remain understandable, upgradeable, and resilient over time.

Design, implement, and maintain secure Solidity smart contracts for lending, borrowing, collateral, liquidation, risk controls, accounting, and protocol governance.

Build modular protocol components and developer tooling that make the system easier to extend, test, monitor, and integrate.

Participate in architecture reviews, code reviews, audit preparation, and remediation of security findings.
Model and simulate adversarial scenarios, including insolvencies, oracle failures, liquidation stress, permissioning failures, and upgrade risks.

You consistently ship code that is clear, well-tested, security-conscious, and easy for others to reason about.
You identify architectural and security risks early, rather than merely implementing tickets as written.
You apply a strong understanding of protocol mechanics, liquidity, and market behavior to identify and mitigate security risks during the design phase, before they reach production.
You become a trusted technical partner to product, risk, and engineering peers on high-stakes protocol decisions.
You help raise the bar for testing, review quality, documentation, and operational discipline across the protocol stack.

4+ years of professional software engineering experience, including 2+ years building EVM-based protocols or financial infrastructure using Solidity.
Demonstrated experience designing, deploying, and maintaining production smart contracts on an EVM-compatible chain.
Deep understanding of Solidity, the EVM, common smart contract vulnerabilities, upgrade and migration patterns, and secure contract design.
Strong hands-on experience with Foundry or equivalent testing frameworks, including fuzzing and invariant testing.
Experience building or contributing to DeFi protocols involving lending, borrowing, collateral, AMMs, vaults, liquidations, staking, or related financial primitives.

Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Prior experience collaborating with external auditors and remediating audit findings.
Familiarity with protocol governance, timelocks, multisigs, emergency controls, and secure deployment processes.

Compound Foundation supports the development, adoption, and responsible growth of Compound - one of DeFi's original lending protocols with over $57B in loans processed - and related decentralized finance tools.
